title: Historical Urban Event Evidence Data Catalog for New York City and London
source_pdf: /mnt/c/Users/ayush/Downloads/Historical Urban Event Evidence Data Catalog for New York City and London.pdf

extraction.note: The raw extracted text is preserved alongside this normalized catalog so no PDF content is discarded.

executive_summary.summary: The catalog identifies the strongest official and quasi-official data sources available through April 2026 for building an open before/after urban event evidence platform for New York City and London.
london_strengths: centralized planning approvals and progress monitoring through Planning London Datahub

new_york: Department of Finance sales and assessment data

executive_summary.time_caveat: 2000–2026 coverage does not mean each series has complete 2026 data. Live APIs can have 2026 records, but many annual surveys and administrative rollups stop in 2024 or 2025. Model event time separately from publication time and preserve source vintage metadata.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: NYC Map Tiles orthophotos and aerial photo history
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: Historic England Aerial Photo Explorer; Environment Agency vertical aerials; OS imagery where licensed
domain_comparison.assessment: NYC has the stronger fully open city orthophoto series for repeated urban comparison. London has strong archival imagery, but less of a single citywide open orthophoto time series and more mixed licensing.
Both cities are equally well served by national and international satellite archives for coarse-grained change detection, heat, land cover, and greenness.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: MapPLUTO/PLUTO, Digital Tax Map, tax lot polygons, 3D building snapshot
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: OS Open UPRN/USRN/Open Roads/OpenMap Local, Planning DataMap, premium OS products, London Building Stock Model v2
domain_comparison.assessment: NYC is stronger for openly reusable parcel and lot-level land-use linkage. London has excellent identifiers and road/network products, but open citywide parcel/building geometry is less straightforward and often depends on premium OS products or derived models.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: ZAP, CEQR Access, BSA records, DOB filings
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: Planning London Datahub, LDD archive, PlanApps, borough planning portals
domain_comparison.assessment: London is stronger for centralized citywide planning lifecycle data and progress tracking. NYC is stronger on construction administration after approval rather than a single unified approvals API.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: Centerline/LION, DOT traffic counts, vehicle classification counts
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: DfT road traffic statistics, OS Open Roads, TfL road and authority layers
domain_comparison.assessment: Both are strong. NYC has good count archives and fine street geometry; London has very strong national traffic count infrastructure and solid road identifiers.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: MTA developer feeds, Bus Time, turnstiles, hourly ridership, stations/entrances
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: TfL Unified API, station topology/facilities, PTAL, Underground performance, network demand, cycle hire
domain_comparison.assessment: NYC is stronger for open station ridership and faregate-based demand data. London is stronger for integrated network metadata and accessibility/topology.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: LEHD/LODES, decennial census, ACS, population estimates
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: ONS census and population estimates, Nomis BRES/APS, GLA borough-by-sector jobs
domain_comparison.assessment: Both are excellent, but the U.S. system is stronger for workplace-residence origin/destination at fine geography, while London is stronger for long-run local jobs series and integrated labour market statistics.

domain_comparison.new_york_priority_source: DOF assessments and sales; HVS and RGB research for rent context
domain_comparison.london_priority_source: HM Land Registry PPD and UK HPI; VOA private rents
domain_comparison.assessment: London is stronger for a unified official property transactions and index stack. NYC is strong on assessment and sales, but rents are more survey/report based than a single transactional feed.

domain_comparison.london_priority_source: PlanApps comments, planning consultations, Talk London, Annual London Survey; no direct 311 equivalent
domain_comparison.assessment: NYC clearly wins on structured complaint exhaust. London has useful opinion and consultation sources, but not a single all-purpose city service-request dataset equivalent to 311.

foundational_sources.coverage_and_gaps: Global archive covers the full 2000–2026 target period and well before it; ideal for long-run urban analysis.
foundational_sources.spatial_granularity: Raster scenes; 30 m multispectral with surface temperature products available.
foundational_sources.recommended_adapter: TILER + scene catalog keyed by path/row and acquisition date
foundational_sources.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best for coarse urban change, heat, vegetation, water, imperviousness, and gap-filling between city orthophoto vintages.

foundational_sources.coverage_and_gaps: Higher-resolution multispectral imagery from 2015 onward; useful for post-2015 seasonal comparisons.
foundational_sources.spatial_granularity: Raster scenes; 10 m/20 m multispectral products.
foundational_sources.license_terms: Copernicus/open data terms; attribution required by product terms.
foundational_sources.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best for more frequent optical monitoring than Landsat after 2015.
notes: The PDF text emphasizes Sentinel as a portable cross-city layer alongside Landsat.

foundational_sources.coverage_and_gaps: Project started 2004; full-history dumps available from 2007 and basic data back to 2005.
foundational_sources.update_frequency: Weekly planet snapshots; minutely diffs for current data.
foundational_sources.license_terms: ODbL with attribution and share-alike duties.
foundational_sources.suggested_use_quality_notes: Essential for historical network/building edits, with contributor-behaviour, survivorship, and completeness biases to label.

city_source_families.source_family: NYC Map Tiles orthophotos and aerial photo history
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Official NYC orthophoto / aerial-photo vintages, strongest repeated open city imagery record for before/after comparison.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Raster tiles and imagery by capture cycle.
city_source_families.update_frequency: Basemap/service updates; imagery by capture cycle.
city_source_families.license_terms: CC BY 4.0.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Gold-standard visual before/after evidence and parcel-adjacent context. Recent vintages are true orthos; older vintages remain valuable context.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Planimetric extraction begins around 2004 and is produced every other ortho capture; 3D building model is explicitly a 2014 snapshot.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Useful for building snapshots and morphology. Confidence high for 3D snapshot, medium for long historical footprint continuity until each vintage is checked.

city_source_families.source_family: PLUTO / MapPLUTO and land-use lot files
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Current PLUTO documentation confirms a rich tax-lot land-use file; historical continuity is strong in practice but every pre-2010 vintage was not verified in the PDF pass.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data unrestricted reuse stated in portal FAQ; verify dataset-level metadata.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Core layer for zoning, built FAR, land use, year built, units, lot area, and BBL linkage.

city_source_families.source_family: Digital Tax Map / tax lot geometry
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Maintained Department of Finance tax map collection with lot, block, and lot-face extracts.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Tax lot, tax block, lot face.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Essential for parcel joins, BBL linkage, and event footprints.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: DOB Job Application Filings are the broad filing ledger; BIS Permit Issuance covers the older system; DOB NOW Build Approved Permits covers most current construction permits.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms.
city_source_families.recommended_adapter: LEDGER + normalized event ontology across filing/issuance/approval
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Core construction-administration stream for filings, permits, and approvals.

city_source_families.source_family: Certificates of occupancy and housing delivery rollups
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: BIS CO covers 2012-07-12 to March 2021; DOB NOW CO takes over after that; DCP Housing Database aggregates approved construction/demolition jobs into housing delivery tables.
city_source_families.update_frequency: Ongoing for CO modules; periodic housing rollups.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best proxy for “building became usable” or “housing units delivered.”

city_source_families.source_family: Zoning, environmental review, and land-use documents
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: ZAP exposes project search and public records; CEQR Access provides environmental review documents; BSA and related records add exception/variance context.
city_source_families.license_terms: Agency site terms; public documents should be handled carefully for personal data.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best for public rationale, consultations, impact studies, mitigation promises, and timelines.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Centerline is the road-bed representation; LION remains the historic all-purpose street database widely used in NYC contexts.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Backbone for geocoding road events, traffic counts, curb changes, and transit links.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: DOT traffic volume counts are historical; vehicle classification counts cover 2011–2025 in the cited dataset.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Good for before/after traffic volume and mode mix. Use repeated nearby stations; do not assume full continuity.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: MTA developer resources cover static feeds, Bus Time, subway/rail service data, GTFS-RT and APIs.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Route, trip, stop, vehicle position, service alert.
city_source_families.format: GTFS, GTFS-RT protobuf, SIRI JSON/XML, REST
city_source_families.license_terms: MTA / Open NY terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Strong for route-change detection, stop inventories, service availability, and live operational overlays.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Annual turnstile usage datasets are open for 2015–2022; hourly subway ridership covers 2020–2024 and 2025 onward in split datasets; daily system ridership covers 2020–2025; OD estimates and station/entrance datasets provide access context.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Station complex, turnstile control area, entrance.
city_source_families.update_frequency: Daily to hourly depending on feed.
city_source_families.license_terms: Open NY terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Powerful for demand deltas, but 2020-era pandemic disruption must be treated as a special context caveat.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Structured service-request ledger from 2010–present.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data has no general restrictions on reuse; privacy care required.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: One of the best public-opinion and nuisance-change proxies available. Minimize exposure of sensitive complaint text/location combinations.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: LEHD/LODES reaches 2002–2022 in published updates; ACS 1-year covers 2005–2024; ACS 5-year covers 2009–2024; decennial APIs cover 2000, 2010, 2020; annual population estimates add city context.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Census tract/block group/place/county and workplace-residence geographies.
city_source_families.license_terms: U.S. Census federal data is generally public domain; preserve Census API terms and margins of error.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Core for jobs, commuting, demographic and socioeconomic baselines.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Annualized citywide sales updates yearly; archives cover prior sales; property valuation/assessment is annual; NYC HVS is triennial and RGB research extends to the 1990s.
city_source_families.license_terms: NYC Open Data terms; survey/report products have their own usage conventions.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: High confidence for sales/assessments; medium-high for rent outcomes because they rely on survey/report families.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Live, citywide planning permissions with progress data; starts and completions are supplied annually by boroughs.
city_source_families.license_terms: Public portal; respect dataset-level terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: London’s single most important urban-event dataset family.

city_source_families.source_family: Planning London Datahub API and schema
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Public API connection documented with JSON returns and Elasticsearch-style search endpoints.
city_source_families.license_terms: Publicly documented access; header required.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Supports direct search by authority, dates, and fields. Excellent for reproducible ETL.

city_source_families.source_family: Residential approvals, starts, completions, and pipeline dashboards
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Current dashboards are derived from PLD; boroughs supply starts and completions annually; dashboard notes warn that inbound data are not fully quality checked at receipt.
city_source_families.update_frequency: Ongoing dashboards and periodic downloadable resources.
city_source_families.license_terms: London Datastore package-level terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best for pipeline and housing-delivery monitoring; preserve borough submission caveats.

city_source_families.source_family: London Development Database archive and planning comments
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: LDD is no longer updated but remains a historical archive; PlanApps supports decisions back to 2012 and lets users comment on live applications; borough planning search pages are linked centrally.
city_source_families.update_frequency: Archived for LDD; current for PlanApps.
city_source_families.license_terms: London Datastore terms; site-specific planning terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best way to bridge older strategic permissions with current mayoral applications and comments.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Broad multi-domain catalog for GLA and partner datasets; package-level licenses vary.
city_source_families.license_terms: Terms vary by package; users must check package license details.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Essential platform layer for production metadata, automated refresh checks, and package discovery.

city_source_families.source_family: Road network, identifiers, and open basemaps
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: OS Open Roads, Open USRN, Open UPRN, OpenMap Local, and Open Zoomstack are current open national layers; not historical time series by themselves.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Road, street identifier, property identifier, general mapping.
city_source_families.license_terms: OS OpenData products use OGL; premium OS products differ.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Important substitute where London parcel/building openness is weaker than NYC.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: OS 3D Mesh beta launched in 2025; London Building Stock Model v2 is a GLA analytical model built over a 2017-based predecessor and updated in-house.
city_source_families.license_terms: OS beta access is not equivalent to unrestricted open data; verify access route.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Useful, but weaker than NYC for a clean open municipal 3D history.

city_source_families.source_family: Historical aerial imagery and vertical aerials
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Historic England Aerial Photo Explorer gives archive access; Environment Agency vertical aerials provide official airborne mapping; OS MasterMap Imagery is authoritative but licensed, not open.
city_source_families.license_terms: Mixed. Historic England image rights vary per image; Environment Agency data are official open-government-style datasets; OS imagery is licensed.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: High value, especially where London lacks a single openly tiled orthophoto series like NYC.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: DfT road traffic statistics provide London count points and raw counts in CSV and JSON; quality notes distinguish “Counted” from “Estimated” methods.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Count point, road link, local authority.
city_source_families.license_terms: UK Open Government Licence for published statistics/data; preserve attribution and method fields.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Always keep estimation method in the model and upweight directly counted observations.

city_source_families.source_family: TfL routes, timetables, accessibility, demand, and cycle hire
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Unified API covers lines, routes, stops, BikePoint, occupancy and more; station facilities/topology and PTAL are available; cycle-hire counts run from 30 July 2010 launch through March 2026 in the cited dataset; some station/journey detail series cover 2003–2012.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Stop, station, line, route, bike point, grid point.
city_source_families.license_terms: TfL terms based on OGL with amendments; check caching/branding/commercial rules.
city_source_families.recommended_adapter: API pull + temporal cache + CUBE snapshots
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Strong for integrated network metadata and accessibility/topology; demand history is less consistently open at station level than NYC.

city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Nomis is the main API/service layer for ONS labour market and census outputs; BRES is the official source of employee/employment estimates; ONS mid-year population estimates provide a 2011–2024 series with older series available; 2001 Census is available through ONS; GLA borough-by-sector jobs spans 1971–2023.
city_source_families.spatial_granularity: Borough, LAD, small areas depending on source.
city_source_families.update_frequency: Annual or quarterly depending on family.
city_source_families.license_terms: Open Government Licence with statistical disclosure controls where applicable.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Very strong for long-run labour and demography.

city_source_families.source_family: Property transactions, price indices, and rents
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: HM Land Registry Price Paid Data is monthly and available from 1995 with yearly files; UK HPI is monthly and linked-data enabled; VOA average private rents are updated biannually and changed cadence after 2013.
city_source_families.license_terms: Official government terms; check Price Paid permitted-use guidance.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Best official stack for property transactions and rent/price trend context.

city_source_families.source_family: Public opinion, consultation, and local sentiment
city_source_families.coverage_and_gaps: Annual London Survey toplines cover 2000–2011 with no survey in 2008; from 2014 onward the Annual London Survey is delivered by Talk London; planning consultations/comments and police dashboards are downloadable through city platforms.
city_source_families.license_terms: Mixed package/site terms.
city_source_families.suggested_use_quality_notes: Useful, but there is no citywide 311-style operational complaint ledger equivalent.

adapter_patterns.description: Imagery and basemap tiling, including city orthophotos and satellite composites.
Annual or periodic full extracts such as PLUTO, PTAL, count-point snapshots, and basemap vintages.
Event streams such as permits, complaints, ridership, certificates, and filings.
Plans, consultation documents, public comments, environmental review documents, and evidence PDFs.
Stable identifiers such as BBL, BIN, station IDs, USRN, UPRN, count points, and road segments.
Statistical datasets, dashboard extracts, API-backed indicators, and geography harmonization.

implementation_guidance.graph_model: Write into a unified spatiotemporal graph keyed by event location, event time, publication time, and source vintage. In NYC, natural keys are often BBL/BIN plus street segment and station complex linkages. In London, practical keys are UPRN/USRN plus LPA application IDs, NaPTAN/StopPoint IDs, or DfT count points.
recommended_visual_products: synchronized before/after image swipe using official imagery
event timeline for filings, approvals, permits, starts, completions, and occupancy
distance-decay charts for traffic, ridership, employment, complaints, and prices
document evidence tab for planning documents, public comments, and environmental statements
implementation_guidance.interpolation_strategy: For missing years, fill imagery gaps with Landsat or Sentinel seasonal composites. For London building-level geometry change, infer windows from PLD/LDD applications, OS/OpenStreetMap baselines, and historic aerials. Treat unreleased 2026 annual series as latest official year plus provisional/live operational context, not as equivalent annual statistics.

legal_ethics_constraints: NYC Open Data broadly states there are no general restrictions on use, but complaint text, addresses, and sensitive topics still create privacy and defamation risk.
TfL data are released under transport-data terms based on the OGL with amendments; check commercial republication, branding, caching, and refresh behavior source by source.
London Datastore licenses vary by package.
OS OpenData products are OGL, but premium OS imagery and some 3D products are not equivalent to open city data.
Historic England imagery can have image-specific rights and attributions.
OpenStreetMap requires attribution and ODbL share-alike treatment for derivative databases.
Planning comments can contain personal data or allegations; minimize personal-text display and prefer aggregation, excerpting, and links over wholesale republication.
open_questions_limitations: London does not have a clean equivalent to NYC lot-level open parcel/building stack or a universal 311-type city service-request ledger.
NYC has strong public administrative and complaint data, but official open rent series are more fragmented than London’s Land Registry plus VOA stack.
Every historical PLUTO/MapPLUTO vintage and every pre-2010 London borough planning archive was not individually verified in the PDF pass.

Start public open-source release with high-confidence official core, mark 2026 annual series as partial, keep a reproducible vintage registry, and add secondary sources only after licensing and continuity are validated.
